nodes.question: Is the link between runoff events and COTS outbreaks definitive?
nodes.answer: No, the link between runoff events and COTS outbreaks is considered equivocal.

nodes.question: What role do reservoirs of juveniles play in COTS outbreaks?
nodes.answer: Reservoirs of juveniles may drive outbreaks through a mechanism known as the juveniles-in-waiting hypothesis, which indicates that juvenile COTS contribute to population increases.
nodes.paragraph: 2023 ; Pratch - ett et al. 2014; Wolfe et al. 2017). The overfishing/preda- tor removal hypothesis posits that adult COTS have been released from predator control (Endean 1969; Kroon et al. 2021). Recent research points to the role that reservoirs of juveniles may have in driving outbreaks, the juveniles-in- waiting hypothesis (Deaker et al. 2020a; Wolfe and Byrne 2024). Given the inherent traits of COTS and plasticity across life stages (Deaker and Byrne 2022), it is likely that many interacting factors across COTS life stages influence outbreaks. Acanthaster begin their benthic life as herbivores. These juveniles are cryptic in the reef infrastructure and are dif- ficult to study (Wilmes et al. 2018, 2020a, b). They feed on crustose coralline algae (CCA) as their preferred food but can subsist on algal films (Deaker et al. 2020b; Lucas 1984 ; Yamaguchi 1973). The juveniles can remain as her - bivores for at least 6.5 years in the absence of coral prey (Deaker et al. 2020a).
